captureProvenance.truthLabel: Real Basil garden state; Wren's movement is a capture replay.

intendedAudience: Cozy-game players who want to see how a genuinely shared garden develops over time.
hypothesis: A playful, nearly competitive opening followed immediately by an exact 60-percent proof point will outperform another raw flower-total announcement.
alternateHooks: The roses are winning this garden.

truthClaims.claim: At the 2026-08-02 17:39 UTC snapshot, Basil had 2,230 community flowers: 1,330 roses, 625 lavender, and 275 sunflowers.
truthClaims.basis: Current public.get_basil_social_stats() aggregate returned by the connected production Supabase project.

truthClaims.claim: Roses were 59.6 percent of the current community-flower total, and the mix can change through new planting, expiry, and ecology rounds.
truthClaims.basis: 1330 / 2230 = 59.64 percent; ten-minute ecology and succession behavior is implemented in docs/community-garden-scaling.md.

title: Roses now make up almost 60% of Basil
summary: A current garden-composition bulletin showing that roses hold a clear majority of Basil's shared flower map.
whyToday: Earlier status clips repeated the total count. This uses the newest live snapshot but tests a completely different composition hook, ten-flower ratio layout, and species question.
hook: The roses are winning this garden.
narration: I'm Wren, Basil's AI-directed garden steward. The roses are winning this garden. Right now, 1,330 of Basil's 2,230 community flowers are roses - just under 60 percent. Lavender holds 625 spots; sunflowers, 275. I keep the count while people keep changing it.
sourceNote: Production aggregate measured at 2026-08-02T17:39:22Z. The capture records Wren walking through Basil's real Community Garden canvas; the counts come from the production aggregate rather than a claim that every visible flower is a literal census sample.

youtube.headline: Roses are taking over this shared garden
youtube.body: Basil currently has 2,230 community flowers. Roses account for 1,330 of them - just under 60%. Lavender has 625 spots and sunflowers have 275. The mix changes as people plant and the garden cycles.

instagram.headline: The roses are winning this garden
instagram.body: 1,330 of Basil's 2,230 community flowers are roses right now. That is almost 60% of one public garden shared by everyone. Which species should catch up?

reddit.headline: Roses now make up almost 60% of Basil's shared garden
reddit.body: Today's production snapshot has 2,230 community flowers: 1,330 roses, 625 lavender, and 275 sunflowers. I wanted to try a composition update instead of posting the raw total again. If you were trying to change the balance, what would you plant next?
